title: A stranger becomes aggressive in public
lede: On a train platform, a man is escalating — over a look, a seat, a phone, nothing. His voice is up, he is stepping into your space, and he wants a reaction from you.

blocks.text: On a train platform, a man is escalating — over a look, a seat, a phone, nothing. His voice is up, he is stepping into your space, and he wants a reaction from you.

items: He is not conducting a negotiation. He is looking for a partner in an incident, and your reply is the invitation. Withholding the reply is the whole skill.
Winning the exchange and being safe are opposite objectives here. Every point you score raises the chance of contact.
Bystanders are frozen by default, not indifferent. They will help if directed specifically, and will not if addressed as "somebody."

items.move: Give him space and a way out
items.detail: Step back and turn slightly side-on. Do not block his exit. Cornered people escalate; people with an exit take it.

items.move: Drop your voice and slow down
items.detail: Match nothing. Volume feeds volume. Slow, quiet speech is genuinely regulating to an agitated person.
The seat, the look, the last word, being right. All cheap. Say sorry for something you did not do and keep your teeth.

items.move: Keep your hands visible and open
items.detail: Nothing in them, nothing sudden. Hands in pockets or behind your back reads as threat and invites pre-emption.
Do not leave the platform for a quiet corridor. Public and observed is protective.
Point and use a description. "You, in the red coat, call the police." Named people act; crowds do not.

items.say: "You're right, my mistake." Costs nothing. Ends a large proportion of these.
"No problem, I'm going." Then go, without a parting shot.
"You in the red coat — call the police, please."
Loud and flat: "Leave me alone." You are now speaking to witnesses, not to him.

items: Eye contact held as a challenge. It is read as an answer to the invitation.
Explaining, correcting, or reasoning. Aggression is not a logic problem.
The phone raised to film as a first move. It commonly triggers the assault it was meant to document. Retreat first, film only from safety.
Standing your ground on principle. Principle is a luxury of environments with consequences.
Any physical contact, including a hand on the chest to keep distance. That is where the legal and physical line moves.
Report it if staff are present, and get an incident number. It matters if he is a repeat presence.
Expect the shake and the delayed anger — often an hour later, often at yourself for not "doing something." You did the correct thing.
Rehearse the concession lines now, out loud. Under adrenaline you use what is rehearsed, not what is wise.

limit: If contact is imminent and you cannot leave, your priorities are: make maximum noise, create distance, put objects between you, and move toward people. Fighting is a last resort with unpredictable outcomes and legal consequences — but if you are being attacked, you are entitled to protect yourself and then leave immediately.
